title: Quantifying Fibrillar Collagen Organization with Curvelet Transform-Based Tools
protocol: Launch the APP as described in section 2.3.
Click on the Open File(s) button in the main graphical user interface (GUI).
Select one or more images/or image stacks from the prompt window using the appropriate technique for the operating system.
Check the Parallel checkbox on the top right corner for multiple images analysis if analyzing multiple images.
Move the slice slider under the file listbox to select the slice to be analyzed for image stack.
Set running properties with default parameters for initial analysis of some images.
If adjusting parameters, click on the Update button in the Parameters panel and follow the manual to properly tune the background threshold (thresh_im2) and nucleation searching radius (s_xlinkbox).
Click on the Run button to start the analysis.
Check the information window and command window for progress details.
After completion, review the output table displayed in the GUI.
Click on any item in the output table to see the histogram of fiber measures including length, width, angle, and straightness.
Examine the fiber images with fibers overlaid on the original image as displayed (Figure 3E).
Check the subfolder named ctFIREout under the image folder for additional output files including the overlaid image “.tiff” file, “.csv” file, and “.mat” file.
Open File(s) button in the main GUI to load one or more images.
Select the image to be annotated in the file list.
Select the ROI Manager from the dropdown menu of ROI Options panel.
Click on the RUN button to launch the ROI Manager module.
In the ROI manager GUI, click on the dropdown menu below Draw ROI Menu(d) to draw ROIs one by one.
Drag the yellow rectangle that appears on the original image to the desired position and then click on the Save ROI(s) button or press s to add this ROI to the ROI list.
Draw a new ROI by dragging the previous ROI to a new position, and save it as mentioned previously.
Press x or select New ROI? in the ROI shape dropdown menu to quit ROI annotation.
Check the Show All and Labels checkboxes to show all defined ROIs on the list and their names on the original image.
Select an ROI from the ROI list to conduct basic operations including Rename ROI, Delete ROI, Save ROI Text, Load ROI from Text, Save ROI Mask, Load ROI from Mask, and Combine ROIs.
Close the ROI manager GUI.
Reset the main GUI by clicking on the Reset button.
Click on one or more ROIs in the ROI list.
Launch the Post-ROI analysis module by clicking on the ctFIRE ROI Analyzer button.
Click on the Check Fibers button to display fibers within the selected ROIs.
Display histograms of each ROI by clicking on Plot Statistics.
Run CT-FIRE analysis directly on the selected ROIs by clicking on the Apply ctFIRE on ROI button if full-image CT-FIRE analysis has not been conducted.
Follow instructions in the prompt window to run the analysis.
Update running parameters as described in step 3.1.5 as needed.
Display summary statistics of fiber measures after analysis completion.
Save results automatically in a subfolder located at \\[image folder]\ CTF_ROI\Individual\ROI_analysis\.
Annotate ROIs for the images to be analyzed according to steps in 3.2.1.
Open one or more images by clicking on the Open File(s) button.
Select CTF post-ROI analyzer from the dropdown menu in the Run Options panel when full image analysis results are available.
Click on the RUN button to run ROI analysis for all loaded images.
Check progress information displayed in the message window at the bottom of the GUI and in the command window.
After analysis is complete, review summary statistics for each ROI displayed in an output table.
Follow steps 3.2.3.1–3.2.3.6 when full image analysis results are not available.
Select CTF ROI analyzer in step 3.2.3.3.
Before clicking RUN button, update running parameters as described in step 3.1.5.
Choose between Rectangular ROI and ROI mask of any shape in a prompt dialog window after clicking RUN button.
Save ROI analysis results in a subfolder located at \\[image folder]\CTF_ROI\Batch\ROI_analysis\.
Launch the CT-FIRE app, or click on the Reset button after other operations to initialize the CT-FIRE main GUI.
Check the .mat checkbox on the top of the main GUI.
Click on the Open File(s) button to select the CT-FIRE output .mat file in the ctFIREout subfolder.
Update the options in the Output Figure Control panel.
Keep the default options in Output Options to ensure all the output files are updated according to new parameters.
Click on the Post-processing button.
Check the progress information in the message window at the bottom of the main GUI as well as in the command window.
Launch the CT-FIRE app or click on the Reset button after other operations to initialize the main GUI.
Check the OUT.adv checkbox at the top of the main GUI.
Click on the Post-processing button to launch the advanced post-processing GUI named “Analysis Module”.
Click on the Select File button to select an image.
Click on the Visualise Fibers button to enter fiber number based on labels in the Original-fibers tab.
Check the thresholding box to enable the threshold settings.
Choose one of the four thresholding options from the dropdown menu.
Enter the desired thresholds in the Thresholds panel for one or more fiber properties.
Click on the Confirm/Update button to move to the thresholding operation.
Click on the Threshold Now button to apply the above thresholding conditions.
Check the prompt figure with its name ending with metrics visualization.
Repeat steps 3.3.2.9–3.3.2.11 to set the desirable thresholds.
Click on the Save Fibers button to save the selected fiber information.
Generate summary statistics by clicking on the Generate stats button.
Click on the OK button in the pop-up window.
Check the Generate sheet for raw data box before clicking on the OK button to include individual fiber information in the output file.
In step 3.3.2.4, check the Batch Mode or Stack Mode and select multiple images or stacks to be analyzed.
Set thresholding conditions in steps 3.3.2.8–3.3.2.9.
Follow the instructions in step 3.3.2.14 to generate summary statistics and individual fiber properties of the selected fibers.
Launch the APP as described in 2.3.
Click on the Reset button to reset the APP to its initial status if other operations have been conducted.
Check the Fiber analysis method option to make sure CT is selected (default option).
Select the boundary processing mode from the following dropdown menu options: No Boundary, CSV Boundary, and TIFF Boundary.
If no boundary is needed, skip this step.
Click on the Get Image(s) button in the main GUI.
Select one or more images or image stacks from the prompt window using appropriate technique for your operating system.
Ensure all selected images are acquired under the same conditions if multiple images are chosen.
For an image stack, select the slice to be analyzed by moving the slice slider under the file listbox.
Enter the Fraction of coefs to keep; this is the fraction of largest coefficients of CT used in fiber analysis.
Annotate regions of interest with even contrast for fiber analysis if there's a large variation in fiber intensity or contrast.
Set a smaller value for the fraction if the image size is larger.
Keep all parameters in Output Options and others in Advanced option as default.
Click on the Run button at the bottom of the main GUI.
Select CT-FIRE Segments to use segments of a fiber to represent the fiber.
Set each segment length to 5 pixels by default in CT-FIRE.
Note the change in orientation along the whole length of the fiber.
In step 4.1.3, select the tiff boundary condition.
Create corresponding boundary files for each image or stack manually using CSV or Tiff format.
Automatically generate boundary files if a pair of H&E bright-field and SHG images are provided.
Enter the distance from the closest boundary in the Primary Parameters panel to evaluate fibers within this range.
Launch the APP as described in section 2.3.
Click on the Reset button to reset the APP to its initial status if other operations have already been conducted.
Click on the BD Creation button to launch the automatic boundary creation module.
Follow the on-screen instructions/clues to create boundary file for one or more images based on a pair of H&E bright-field and SHG images.
Close the module window, or click on the Reset button in the main GUI to quit this module.
Click on the Get Image(s) button in the main GUI to load one or more images.
Select the image to be annotated in the file list.
Click on the ROI Manager to launch the ROI Manager module.
Follow steps 3.2.1.5–3.2.1.13 in section 3.2.1 for ROI annotation using ROI Manager.
If full image CurveAlign analysis has been conducted, and the results are saved in the default directory, click on one or more ROIs in the ROI list.
Click on the CA ROI Analyzer button to run Post-ROI analysis.
After the analysis is complete, summary statistics will be displayed in an output table as well as a histogram figure showing the angle distribution.
Wait for the estimated running time for processing an image with size 1024 pixels x 1024 pixels with moderate fiber density.
Consider factors such as file size, analysis mode, features deployed, CPU type, and available RAM when estimating computational time.
CT-FIRE individual fiber extraction takes a couple of minutes.
CurveAlign CT-mode without boundary takes a few seconds.
CurveAlign CT-FIRE fiber or fiber ends mode without boundary takes tens of seconds.
CurveAlign CT-FIRE fiber mode without boundary takes hundreds of seconds.
CurveAlign analysis with boundary takes tens of seconds to several minutes, depending on the complexity of the boundaries.
